# CoperativeAI — how work is done here

A desktop workspace where Product, Developers and QA plan, build and test
software cooperatively with AI, built with the CooperativeAICoding framework in
this same repository.

## Where the code lives

| Solution | Type | Local path |
|---|---|---|
| CoperativeAI | Tauri application — Rust backend, React 19 + TypeScript frontend | `app/CoperativeAI` |
| CoperativeAIdb | turso database, embedded in the application | `app/CoperativeAI/db` |

The framework's own material is separate: `template/` is the blank copy,
`example/` a worked project, `application/` this app's real briefs, `site/` the
published documentation, `tools/` the checks, `bin/` the `init` CLI.

`application/ai-only/` is the AI's workspace for this app. Build from the
approved spec at `application/ai-only/<solution>/<item>.md`, take project-wide
constraints from the Project Digest in `application/ai-only/Project_system.md`,
and append your round report to the item's spec.

## House rules, as this project defines them

- **DRY** — if code repeats three times, move it into a shared method or module
  and reuse it. The name of the rule is not the rule; this sentence is.
- **SOLID** — single responsibility, dependency injection and interfaces where
  practical. Changes to production code stay **small**, or the code is extended
  by a new version file rather than reworked in place.
- **Keep it simple** — enough code to finish the job, and no more.
- **TDD** — write a failing test, then just enough code to pass it. Tests start
  simple and grow with the functionality.
- **Reuse before building.** `application/ai-only/Code_map.md` lists every
  method already built, what it does, and what it uses. Check it before writing
  anything new, and update the row for any method you create or change — the
  same build that changes a method fixes its row. `node tools/code-map-lint.mjs`
  checks the map still matches the code.

## Security

Single-user local app, no authentication. API keys and the GitHub token live in
the OS credential store via `keyring`; only aliases and URLs go in the database.
AI policies are **deny-by-default** and checked before every AI call. Roles
decide what is visible, and are **not** an access-control boundary — the app
says so itself rather than implying protection it does not have.

**Secret values are never written into code, config, logs or documents.**
Reference them by name.

## Testing

Gates that must pass: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (warnings are
failures), `cargo test`, `tsc --noEmit`, `npm test`. Run them from
`app/CoperativeAI` and its `src-tauri` manifest.

**The project has not yet answered what level of cover a change must reach.**
The brief asks for it (`testing`) and the answer is blank, so use the TDD rule
above and say in your round record what you did not test. Do not invent a
threshold.

## What we are working towards

In order. The first is the one everything is currently building towards.

1. **MVP — the cooperative loop, end to end.** Done when a work item can go
   from planned by Product, to planned and approved by Develop, to built by an
   agent in a bounded workspace, to reviewed and merged, to covered by a QA
   test case, without leaving the app.
2. **Agent governance.** Done when what an agent may read, edit and reach is
   decided per work item and enforced rather than requested: deny-by-default
   policy, the sandbox boundary, per-file agent policy, and the MCP server as
   the enforcement layer rather than a prompt.
3. **Feature Designer.** Done when Product can lay a feature out on the
   drag-and-drop canvas, and the design it produces is what generates the work
   items.

When the last item naming a deliverable is built, **stop there** and say the
deliverable is complete, rather than starting the next one.

**These are drafted, not yet accepted.** The brief's answer still carries the
`drafted · guessed` marker: the names, the split and the order were inferred
from what has been built. Treat them as the working target, but if an item's
work does not fit any of them, say so rather than picking one. Most item briefs
do not yet name a deliverable at all.

## The working agreement

- Build the **smallest thing** that answers the request. No unrequested extras.
- Treat existing code as **working in production**, even if it looks broken.
- **Never invent scope.** Anything the brief does not say is an open question,
  not a decision you get to make.
- **When you cannot understand something, stop and say so.** A guess that
  becomes code is the failure this whole way of working exists to prevent.
  Saying "I do not know how you want this done" is the most useful thing you can
  write, not an admission of failure.
- A person reviews and approves a plan before code is written.

## When you finish, write this down

Append to `ROUND-RECORD.md`, one heading each:

### What I did
### What I could not do  (and what you would need to tell me)
### Debt I left behind  (one paragraph each, so each can become its own work item)

Debt that is not written down is debt that gets paid by surprise. One paragraph
per item, because each one becomes a work item somebody owns.

## What this file cannot give you

These are the rules, not the machinery. Plan approval before code is written,
model and effort per work item, what a run cost, deny-by-default policy per item
and a bounded place for agents to run all live in the CoperativeAI app and its
commands. With another agent you get the guardrails and the briefs; enforcing
the rest is on you.
